summary: I went after the one limitation I had recorded against the VerifyLeader finding — that its practical exposure was argued from the lease rather than measured — and submitted a retained probe for it as a child question. The probe partitions the leader together with the nonvoter on a real three-voter plus one-nonvoter cluster, polls the exported verification path while the leader is still confirmable, then keeps watching until the detached voters elect their own leader, so the last confirmation and the competing leader land on one clock along with the competing leader's commit index and the cut-off leader's applied index; the control repeats it with the nonvoter cut off as well. Two comparisons declare the prediction (the confirmation precedes the competing leader, i.e. the lease closes the window before an overlap can form) and the control (no confirmations at all without the nonvoter's acknowledgement). Native feedback from the local dry run, explicitly not retained evidence and the reason this is worth a receipt: with the captured timers the cut-off leader confirmed nine times in a row, the last at 47ms, then stepped down, while the detached voters' leader did not appear until 121ms — a clean separation, not an overlap — and the control produced zero confirmations with the competing leader appearing at 125ms. If the retained run shows the same separation, the honest consequence is to narrow the finding rather than the mechanism: the defect stays that a confirmation is satisfied by an acknowledgement from a server that cannot vote, so it cannot distinguish a leader that still reaches a voter majority from one that does not, while the stale-read outcome would require a timing relation this configuration does not produce. I registered the child question with that discriminator, so the next step is to interpret its receipt and correct the parent account accordingly instead of inheriting the stronger reading.
